verses.author: model_A
verses.text: My grandmother's hands remember a language I never learned.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
flour on the counter
holds the shape of her palms
after she's gone to bed

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
morning light finds
the same white handprints—
I set my own hands there

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the dough remembers
what I press into it now
warm, and rising still

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
not her voice, not mine—
this small yeast breathing
between our two silences

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
outside the window
crows argue over nothing
the bread doesn't care

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
flour on the sill
where her mother's hand once rested
I leave mine there too

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the oven ticks warm
counting hours we don't speak of
what rises, rises

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
morning light finds
the same crack in the counter
we never fixed, still holding

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
steam fogs the window
someone's initials, years old
still spell a name back

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the kettle knows
its way to boil without me
some habits keep us

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the drawer sticks again
where we keep what we don't use
still, we keep it

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the calendar's wrong month
still tacked to the wall
we like the picture too much to turn it

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
dust on the picture frame
we mean to clean it someday
today isn't someday yet

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the porch light left on
all night for no one coming
just in case they do

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the kettle sings twice
once for the tea we forgot
once for the wanting
